name: Jenbach
kurzbeschreibung: Railway hub at the entrance to the Zillertal, featuring the historic Achenseebahn and Schloss Tratzberg.
beschreibung:
Overview

Jenbach is situated at an elevation of 530 metres in the Lower Inn Valley in the district of Schwaz, strategically nestled on the alluvial fan of the Kasbach stream beneath the Karwendel and Rofan mountain ranges. Home to roughly 7,550 residents, this bustling market town is the third-largest municipality in the district. Standing at the junction where the Inn Valley meets both the Zillertal and Lake Achensee, Jenbach serves as the strategic tourist gateway to two of Tyrol's premier holiday valleys. The town merges proud mining and industrial traditions with exceptional transport infrastructure. Globally renowned among railway enthusiasts, Jenbach railway station is the only station in the world where three different track gauges converge in regular passenger service, complemented by the Renaissance splendour of Tratzberg Castle and the scenic hiking paths of the Kasbach Gorge.

History

The settlement was first officially documented in 1269 as Umbaych or Jenpach, meaning "beyond the brook". During the 15th and 16th centuries, Jenbach flourished in the wake of the booming silver and copper mining operations in neighbouring Schwaz, harnessing the water power of the Kasbach for blast furnaces and iron hammer mills. From the 17th century onwards, it evolved into an international centre of scythe manufacture, eventually spawning the Jenbacher Werke (today INNIO Jenbacher, a global leader in industrial gas engines). Rail transport cemented Jenbach's international profile: In 1858, standard-gauge rail (1,435 mm) arrived; in 1889, the meter-gauge Achenseebahn (1,000 mm) opened as Europe's oldest purely steam-operated cog railway; and in 1902, the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn (760 mm) followed. Perched nearby is Castle Tratzberg, expanded around 1500 by Emperor Maximilian I into an architectural jewel.

Getting There

Jenbach is one of the most accessible travel hubs in the Eastern Alps. Motorists arrive smoothly via the Inntal Motorway A12 taking either the "Jenbach" exit or the "Wiesing/Zillertal/Achensee" interchange onto the federal highway B171. Train passengers enjoy comprehensive high-speed rail connections: Jenbach station is a regular stop for Austrian and German Railjet, ICE, Eurocity, and Nightjet services from Vienna, Munich, Zurich, and Frankfurt, reinforced by Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5. Directly from the platforms, passengers can transfer to the Zillertal Railway, the Achensee cog railway, and regional bus routes.

Tips

A ride on the historic Achenseebahn is an unforgettable highlight: Since 1889, original steam locomotives have powered passengers up the steep incline directly to the boat docks of Lake Achensee. Another scenic option is riding the nostalgic steam trains of the Zillertalbahn. Above the valley, tour Castle Tratzberg to admire its lavish Renaissance staterooms, the Habsburg Hall with its monumental family tree mural, and child-friendly audio tours. Heritage buffs will appreciate the Jenbacher Museum, chronicling railway history, early scythe forging, and engine innovation. For hikers, the shaded Kasbach Gorge trail leads through rushing cascades up to Eben am Achensee.
